term: finite causal history and per se regress
resolution: FiniteDistinctAncestry counts distinct upstream relata via nonempty finite paths in a supplied cause relation. NoCausalLoops excludes revisiting a relatum and is independent of that count: a finite self-loop is the omission model. Accessibility forbids infinite descending histories, including repetitions, but allows infinitely many independent immediate causes. PerSeLinksIncluded is the explicit same-carrier restriction to Aquinas’s per se efficient-cause link. There is no automatic identity between causal-power events in Koons and efficient causes as beings in Aquinas. A broadly quantified finitism covering accidental series would exclude infinite accidental ancestry, whereas Aquinas I q.46 a.2 ad 7 does not regard such regress as impossible; neither reading is rewritten to identify the two. No possible-world quantifier or temporal length bound is formalized; the new premises are unattributed open hypotheses. See docs/notes/causal-finitism-367.md.
